status: exact trace/off-diagonal and centered Brownian-bridge Vaughan reduction with one open two-component gate

rows.statement: For 0<alpha<1 set q_n=mu(n)n^(-1-alpha), r_N=sum_(n>N)q_n, and R_alpha=sum_(N>=1)N^alpha|r_N|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: These are the checked reciprocal-Mobius tail coordinates.

rows.statement: For dyadic K let y_j=r_(K+j-1), c_(K,r)=<y,phi_r>, and E_alpha=sum_(K dyadic)K^alphasum_(0<=r<K)|c_(K,r)|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: The Neumann DCT basis is that of Lemma 11.22V.

rows.statement: Define h_(K,0)(n)=K^(-1/2)min((n-K)_+,K), and for 1<=r<K define h_(K,r)(K+m)=sqrt(2/K)sin(pi*r*m/K)/[2sin(pi*r/(2K))] for 1<=m<K, with zero values elsewhere.
rows.proof_boundary: The mean kernel includes every future dyadic block; each nonconstant kernel is supported on (K,2K).
Count the number of tails containing q_n for r=0 and use the checked sine formula for r>0.

rows.statement: Let A_alpha x have coordinates K^(alpha/2)sum_n x_n n^(-1-alpha)h_(K,r)(n) over dyadic K and 0<=r<K.
rows.proof_boundary: For x_n=mu(n), ||A_alpha x||_2^2=E_alpha.
On K<=N<2K, the weights N^alpha and K^alpha differ by at most the fixed factor 2^alpha.
Split K<n<=2K from n>2K and compare the latter decreasing series with its integral.
Use sum_(m=1)^(K-1)sin^2(pi*r*m/K)=K/2 and sin(pi*r/(2K))>=r/K.
Rows 7-8 give at most [1+2^(-1-2alpha)/(1+2alpha)+pi^2/24]sum_K K^(-alpha).

rows.statement: For a finite dyadic cutoff J, E_alpha(J)=D_alpha(J)+2O_alpha(J), where D is the m=n part and O=sum_(m<n)mu(m)mu(n)G_(alpha,J)(m,n) for the Gram kernel G=sum_(K<=2^J,r)K^alpha F_(K,r)(m)F_(K,r)(n).
rows.proof_boundary: Each finite-J row is l1, so the displayed expansion is absolutely justified before taking J to infinity.
The diagonal D_alpha(J) converges by row 9 and E_alpha(J) is a monotone nonnegative partial energy.

rows.statement: A_alpha is Hilbert-Schmidt from l2(N) to the dyadic DCT coefficient space, while the RH input mu is not in l2.
rows.proof_boundary: The squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is exactly the trace in row 9; this operator fact alone does not evaluate A_alpha mu.

rows.statement: A_alpha is not bounded from l_infinity to l2.
rows.proof_boundary: The zero-mean first-mode sequence of Lemma 11.22W gives |x_n|=|q*_n n^(1+alpha)|<=1 but divergent output energy. It is not the Mobius sequence.
Both paths start at zero and T is the weighted path from Lemma 11.22W.
This is the Euclidean quotient norm modulo constants.
For S_(K,0)=0, A_K S_K=T_K exactly.

rows.statement: A_K(c1)=a_1 c1, so A_K induces an invertible operator on the quotient by constants.
rows.proof_boundary: All a_m are nonzero; the increment relation Delta(A_Kx)_m=a_m Delta x_m gives invertibility.
Use the diagonal-plus-prefix Abel matrix, a_m<=K^(-1-alpha), a_m-a_(m+1)<=(1+alpha)K^(-2-alpha), and prefix norm <=K.
This is finite summation of Delta x_m=b_m Delta y_m.
Use b_m<=(2K)^(1+alpha), b_(m+1)-b_m<=(1+alpha)(2K)^alpha, and prefix norm <=K.
Rows 17-20 descend to quotient norms; no DCT-commutator estimate is needed.
This is the centered-path Parseval identity from Lemma 11.22W.
For r>0, tau=-c; apply the checked high-mode bound from Lemma 11.22V.

rows.statement: sum_K K^alpha sum_(1<=r<R_K)|tau_(K,r)|^2<infinity iff L_alpha:=sum_K K^(-2-alpha)||[S_K]||_K^2<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: Add the summable high modes, then apply the two-sided quotient estimate in row 21.

rows.statement: R_alpha<infinity iff M_alpha+L_alpha<infinity, where M_alpha=sum_K K^alpha|sqrt(K)r_K-tau_(K,0)|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: Compose row 24 with the exact two-component criterion of Lemma 11.22W.

rows.statement: For any fixed cofinal alpha_j->0, RH iff M_(alpha_j)<infinity and L_(alpha_j)<infinity for every j.
rows.proof_boundary: This is a criterion only; neither component is estimated.
Use the standard finite variance/pairwise-distance identity.
The kernel is the discrete Brownian-bridge Green matrix L^*(I-K^(-1)11^T)L.
Separate i=j and write j=i+h.
The diagonal series converges by row 30 and the partial bridge energies are nonnegative and monotone.

rows.statement: Green and Tao, Lemma 4.1, give the finite Vaughan Type I/II identity for sum_(K<n<=2K)mu(n)f(n).
rows.proof_boundary: Only the exact divisor identity is imported; no bound for the present shifted-Mobius tests is attributed to the source.

rows.statement: For 1<=h<=K-2 and i=n-K define g_(K,h)(n)=mu(n+h)i(K-i-h)/K when 1<=i<=K-1-h, and zero otherwise; |g_(K,h)|<=K/4.
rows.proof_boundary: Then C_K=sum_h sum_(K<n<=2K)mu(n)g_(K,h)(n).
These are the coefficients in the finite Vaughan identity.

rows.statement: With TI_K=sum_h sum_(d<=U_KV_K)a_(K,d)sum_(K/d<w<=2K/d)g_(K,h)(dw), and the corresponding TII_K=sum_h sum_(V_K<d<=2K/U_K)b_(K,d)sum_(max(U_K,K/d)<w<=2K/d)mu(w)g_(K,h)(dw), one has C_K=-TI_K+TII_K.
rows.proof_boundary: Apply Vaughan termwise in h; invalid endpoint values vanish by the definition of g.
Substitute row 35 into the exact off-diagonal criterion.

rows.statement: The target in row 36 retains the signed Type I/II difference; replacing it by |TI_K|+|TII_K| is not an equivalent reduction.
rows.proof_boundary: The algebraic cancellation in Vaughan is part of the original Mobius sum and no absorbable separate bound is proved.

rows.statement: Averaged Chowla gives the natural unweighted average o(K^2) after collapsing the redundant shift average, but the Brownian-bridge weight is O(K), leaving o(K^3), one full power above the K^(2+epsilon) scale required here.
rows.proof_boundary: This is exponent bookkeeping for the published averaged theorem, not a lower bound on C_K or a novelty claim.

rows.statement: The centered bridge removes constants and therefore does not control M_alpha; both components in row 25 remain necessary. The reduction concerns R_alpha, not the full Burnol energy Q.
rows.proof_boundary: No centered-path estimate may be promoted to RH without the affine mean series or an independently sufficient full-Q theorem.

rows.statement: For every alpha in one fixed cofinal sequence, prove both the affine mean summability M_alpha<infinity and the signed Brownian-bridge/Vaughan criterion in row 36.
rows.proof_boundary: No Type I/II power gain, mean estimate, full Burnol bound, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda<=0 is proved.
